concepts.def: God taking human form in Jesus — fully God, fully human
Jesus' death repairs the rift between God and humanity
Jesus rose from the dead on the third day
Jesus returned to heaven 40 days after resurrection
Free, unearned gift of God's love

walkthroughs.body_html:
The incarnation is God becoming human in Jesus.

John 1:14 — 'The Word became flesh and dwelt among us.'

Jesus is fully God and fully human — defined by the Council of Chalcedon (451 CE). Christmas celebrates this miracle of God-with-us (Emmanuel).

Jesus was crucified under Pontius Pilate. For Christians it was not a defeat — it was atonement.

Sin broke the relationship with God. Jesus' death repairs it (Romans 5:8).

Different views: penal substitution (Jesus took our punishment), moral example (showing God's love), Christus Victor (defeating evil). All point to the cross as central.

On the third day Jesus rose from the dead — Easter Sunday. The empty tomb and appearances convinced the disciples.

40 days later he ascended to heaven. 10 days after that, the Spirit came at Pentecost.

Ephesians 2:8 — 'By grace you have been saved through faith.' Salvation is a free gift, received through trust in Jesus, leading to good works.

mcqs.q: The Council of Chalcedon (451 CE) defined Jesus as:

options: The coming of the Holy Spirit
